rv.q: David Constantine’s short story turned film is a quiet and delicate thing. So much of its emotion happens in the unspoken moments and silent revelations. What a tricky business to transpose this to the stage, so it is impressive that Hannah Patterson adapts with such spare, evocative economy.
Gabriel Byrne and Geraldine James star in this bleak and brittle character study about the persistence of grief and the power of enduring love

The play is equipped with a star cast and interesting material, but frustratingly never reaches its full potential and left me feeling like I just watched a distinctly average play. The show is based on the 2015 film of the same name by Andrew Haigh, which itself is based on David Constantine’s short story In Another Country .
